title: Stowmarsh Therapeutics VPC onramp — field digest
content:
Context:
- Customer: Stowmarsh Therapeutics (small biotech, clinical-grade data, US+EU presence). Trying to move from proof-of-concept (hosted API) to private VPC deployment for PHI-sensitive inference. They want a hybrid onramp: initial VPC peering to a limited set of endpoints, then a fully private control plane later.
- Call: 2025-11-05 technical kickoff with Stowmarsh infra, security, and ML engineering. Internal attendees: Priya (SE), Ethan (infra), Marta (security). Customer attendees: Lena (infra lead), Omar (ML infra), Priya R. (privacy officer).

High-level asks from customer:
1) Bring-up a Private Redwood control plane in their VPC (initially limited functionality: model hosting, inference; no auto-scaling during POC).
2) Model and data residency guarantees — workloads and logs must stay in customer VPC; minimal egress.
3) KMS integration: support customer-managed CMKs (AWS KMS) for model artifacts and audit logs.
4) Network controls: mTLS for control plane <-> runtime, SSH jump/bastion for admin, strict security groups, VPC flow logs to their SIEM.
5) Latency SLO targets: 95th percentile <= 220ms for 512-token responses for their most critical route.
6) Deployment window: POC (6–8 weeks), then production readiness review after 3 months.

Notes from the technical discussion (raw):
- Architecture options discussed: fully private control plane (customer-hosted) vs. hybrid (Redwood control plane + private runtime). They prefer hybrid with eventual full private control plane.
- KV cache persistence: Omar emphasized that warm-up of key-value cache across restarts causes spikes. For their clinical assistants they need stable latencies under burst traffic (lab results ingestion). We flagged: persistent on-disk KV cache per model variant would help but needs reconciliation during rollouts.
- GPU profile: they plan to use 2x A10G-equivalent nodes (on-prem style) initially. Memory budget per host is tight (40–48GB usable). Recommended model configs: trimmed Llama-2.1 7B quantized 4-bit / Redwood-optimized kernels. Must test memory footprint with 4k context and batch=6.
- Disk: models ~8–12GB (7B q4), KV cache disk growth unpredictable — plan 200GB SSD per host as safe default.
- Egress: they will not allow outbound internet from runtime nodes except to Redwood control plane IPs for license/updates. Need to document exact endpoints and port ranges.
- KMS: support for envelope encryption and separate CMK for artifacts vs. logs. Stowmarsh legal wants key rotation policy in writing.
- Audit logs: must ship detailed token-level usage and per-request prompt hashes to their SIEM. Agreed to provide a log format sample (we to deliver).
- Healthchecks and long streaming: They use long-lived streaming sessions (clinical dialogue). We warned about LB idle timeouts causing stream resets; suggested configuring LB for 10+ minute idle and keepalive pings.
- Model pinning / rollouts: They want deterministic pin -> scheduling policy with canary traffic split and instant fallback to hosted variants if runtime capacity exhausted. Need an explicit fallback policy doc.

Identified gotchas / risk items (prioritized):
1) KV cache warm-start spikes: cold cache requests can blow the 95th latency. Action: measure cold vs warm in benchmark harness and give guidance (prefill strategies, smaller prefix cache TTL).
2) Quantization compatibility with the customer's inference toolchain (they plan internal monitoring on GPU telemetry). We must validate Redwood-compiled kernels on their GPU image (driver/CUDA version matrix).
3) Network egress policy mismatch: their security team may block package updates which could break runtime image pulls. Need an offline image bundle option.
4) Billing & metering: they require per-tenant token metering and daily usage exports to S3 with KMS encryption. Confirmed we can produce S3 exports but need to wire permissions.
5) Onprem GPU driver mismatches: one-time operational flakiness when customers bring custom AMIs. Recommend our reference AMI + step-by-step image validation checklist.
6) Long-running streams and autoscaler interplay: autoscaler killing underlying pod during active stream -> partial responses lost. Recommend sticky routing and stream-aware drain.

Concrete follow-ups (owners + deadlines):
- Deliver explicit endpoint list and ports for minimal outbound egress (Priya) — due 2025-11-09.
- Benchmark: run their 512-token, batch=6 profile on our internal harness targeting A10G-equivalent; report cold/warm 50/95/99 latencies and memory/disk usage (Ethan) — due 2025-11-15.
- Draft KMS envelope flow + rotation doc and sample IAM policy for their CMKs (Marta + Priya) — due 2025-11-12.
- Produce sample audit log export (token meta + hashed prompt) and example S3 export manifest (Ethan) — due 2025-11-12.
- Create offline image bundle instructions and verify image pull w/o internet (Dev) — due 2025-11-16.
- Fallback / rollout policy draft: canary routing + instant fallback + version pinning options (Priya) — due 2025-11-13.

Quick checklist to take into the next call (clean, short):
- Bring endpoint whitelist + control-plane domain list.
- Confirm GPU driver / CUDA version they run (AMI details).
- Agree exact SLO route names and latency measurement window for contract.
- Get list of internal teams that need RBAC on control plane UI.
- Ask if they need offline model fetching (air-gapped) for final production.

Testing / validation plan (high level):
- Phase 0 (pre-provision): confirm AMI + kernel matrix, exchange KMS test key, confirm S3 bucket + IAM role for logs.
- Phase 1 (POC deploy): deploy single-node runtime, small model (7B q4), run synthetic traffic (5–10 TPS) with mix of streaming and non-streaming sessions, measure latencies and KV cache behavior.
- Phase 2 (scale test): run 2-node cluster, batch=6, intermittent cold restarts, simulate canary rollouts, validate fallback to hosted.
- Phase 3 (handoff): document runbook for upgrades, key rotation, incident playbook for stream resets and failed rollbacks.

Notes to self (informal):
- Avoid promising auto-scaling within POC window — they keep asking; say clearly: "no autoscale for POC, but we can do manual vertical scaling and do smoke tests".
- For latency targets we should call out that 95p includes downstream KS accesses (if KV cache misses) — get explicit language from product for contractual SLO.
- Consider shipping a tiny prefill agent (small background job that warms KV cache for top-20 prompts) as a low-effort improvement if cold cache becomes an issue.

Possible docs/assets to prepare before next sync:
- Minimal egress endpoint list (1-pager).
- KMS envelope flow + IAM policy example (markdown).
- POC deployment checklist (step-by-step runbook).
- Sample audit log schema + example 100-line export.
- Lightweight prefill job prototype (script).

Next call: schedule in 1 week to review benchmarks and KMS policy draft. Propose 2025-11-13 11am PT. Action: Priya to propose via email and include agenda.

Raw call transcript highlights (scrappy):
- Lena: "We can't have model weights leave our VPC — full stop."
- Omar: "Latency variance kills clinician trust; if it spikes we need automatic failover to hosted variant with tracing."
- Privacy officer PR: "We need per-request retention policy and an option to redact prompts in logs before export."

End of notes. Keep in this file as working record for the SE handoff. Will move selected parts to Confluence after action items resolved.
